title: Joi Farm

cover.alt: Joi Farm dairy product range — milk, ghee, yogurt, lassi and pancer packaging

gallery.alt: Full Joi Farm dairy lineup styled with mango, lychee and almonds
Joi Farm regular milk, ghee, yogurt and lassi on a blue gradient backdrop

summary: A full dairy product line rendered CGI-first, from single hero bottles to a complete shelf lineup.
description: Joi Farm needed consistent, photoreal packaging renders across an entire dairy range — milk, ghee, yogurt, pancer and lassi — without a physical shoot for every SKU. Each product was modeled and lit to match the brand's blue-and-white identity, then composited into styled scenes with fruit, nuts and floral props for marketing and e-commerce use.

title: The Oberoi Patisserie

cover.alt: The Oberoi Patisserie packaging system — gift boxes, cake boxes, cups and menus

gallery.alt: Full Oberoi Patisserie packaging suite laid out with illustrated ribbon motifs

summary: A luxury patisserie identity carried across boxes, cups, coasters and menus.
description: A cohesive packaging system for a New Delhi patisserie — gift boxes in a signature multi-colour palette, take-away cups with playful coffee lines, and menus tied together by a recurring circus-inspired illustration. Every piece was mocked up in 3D to test proportion, colour and finish before print.

title: thaan

cover.alt: thaan fashion brand packaging with heritage photography and business cards

gallery.alt: thaan box, lookbook and stationery styled together

summary: "Heritage threads, modern vision" — a fashion brand's packaging built around archival photography.
description: thaan pairs handwoven Indian textiles with a contemporary silhouette, and the packaging needed to hold both halves of that story. Archival riverfront photography anchors the box interior while a restrained monochrome exterior and bilingual wordmark carry the brand across stationery, hang tags and lookbook pages.

title: District by Zomato

cover.alt: Stadium stage at night surrounded by oversized fantastical planets

gallery.alt: Concert stadium with glowing planets suspended above the crowd
Gateway of India reimagined as the District by Zomato event entrance

summary: Speculative CGI keyframes for Zomato's District events — landmark venues rebuilt as surreal stages.
description: Two keyframes exploring how District by Zomato could take over real Indian landmarks — a stadium engulfed in oversized planets for a night show, and the Gateway of India rebuilt into a glowing event gate. Built to sell the scale and mood of live event marketing before a single physical build begins.

title: Furlicks

cover.alt: Stacked Furlicks pet supplement oral strip boxes in bright flavor-coded colors

gallery.alt: Full Furlicks range — gut health, hip & joint, calming, skin & coat and multivitamin strips

summary: A color-coded pet supplement range rendered as a single stacked product wall.
description: Furlicks needed its oral-strip supplement range — gut health, hip & joint, calming, skin & coat, multivitamin and fresh breath — to read instantly by category. Each box was rendered with consistent studio lighting and stacked into one hero composition so the full line could be understood at a glance.

gallery.alt: Red and black customized cars under city streetlights for the Indian Sneaker Festival

summary: A night-city street standoff built to promote the Indian Sneaker Festival.
description: A key visual pairing custom-lit sports cars with bold street typography, staged in a photoreal city environment to capture the energy of the Indian Sneaker Festival's automotive and streetwear crossover.

title: Studio Bottle Study

cover.alt: A single glass bottle backlit in near-total darkness on a stone ledge

gallery.alt: Silhouetted bottle study with dramatic rim lighting

summary: A lighting exercise in restraint — one bottle, one rim light, near-total darkness.
description: A personal lighting study built to push contrast and silhouette rather than surface detail — a single glass bottle rim-lit against a stone ledge, testing how little information is needed for a product to still read clearly.
